jobs.title: Security Officer Part Time Loss Prevention Driver
jobs.description:
Overview

Allied Universal®, North America’s leading security and facility services company, offers rewarding careers that provide you a sense of purpose. While working in a dynamic, welcoming, and collaborative workplace, you will be part of a team that contributes to a culture that positively impacts the communities and customers we serve.

Job Description

As a Security Officer Part Time Loss Prevention Driver in Dallas, TX, you will serve and safeguard clients in a range of industries such as Retail/Malls, and more. Join a leading team where flexibility meets opportunity. As a Part-Time Security Officer, you can build a schedule that works for you and explore new roles using our Claim a Shift platform. Learn more: aus.com/earnmore. As a Patrol Unarmed Officer at a retail location, you will conduct routine patrols, maintain a visible presence to help deter security-related incidents, and provide outstanding customer service. This driving post requires a valid driver's license. You will communicate professionally with customers and team members while supporting a welcoming environment. Join Allied Universal, where agility, reliability, innovation, teamwork, caring, and integrity guide our work.

Position Type: Part Time

 Pay Rate: $17.00 / Hour

Job Schedule

DayTimeMon12:00 PM - 04:00 PMSun12:00 PM - 12:00 AM

What You'll Do

  • Provide customer service to customers, visitors, and store personnel by carrying out security-related procedures, site-specific policies, and, when appropriate, emergency response activities.
  • Respond to incidents, customer concerns, and critical situations in a calm, professional, problem-solving manner.
  • Conduct regular and random unarmed patrols throughout the retail sales floor, entrances, parking areas, receiving areas, and perimeter to help to deter unauthorized activity.
  • Monitor access points and observe customer and employee activity for unusual conditions, reporting concerns according to site-specific procedures.
  • Document incidents, observations, and patrol activities accurately and communicate relevant information to appropriate personnel.

Minimum Requirements

  • A valid driver’s license is required in accordance with Allied Universal driver policy requirements.
  • Loss prevention experience is preferred.
  • Be at least 18 years of age for unarmed roles; 21+ years of age for armed roles.
  • Possess a high school diploma or equivalent.
  • As a condition of employment, applicants will be subject to a background investigation in accordance with all federal, state, and local laws.
  • Allied Universal will consider qualified applications with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable laws.
  • As a condition of employment, applicants will be subject to a drug screen to the extent permitted by law.
  • Licensing requirements are subject to state and/or local laws and regulations and may be required prior to employment.
  • A valid driver’s license will be required for driving positions only.

Why Join Us

  • Smart Tools: Access to our exclusive technology to view and claim additional shifts to earn more.
  • Career Growth: Get paid training and access to career growth opportunities.
  • Financial Benefits: Participate in our retirement savings plan to invest in your future.
  • Exclusive Perks: Enjoy discounts on top brands and services through our Perks Program.

Closing

Allied Universal® is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race/ethnicity, age, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, genetic information, disability, protected veteran status or relationship/association with a protected veteran, or any other basis or characteristic protected by law. For more information: www.aus.com.

If you have difficulty using the online system and require an alternate method to apply or require an accommodation, please contact our local Human Resources department. To find an office near you, please visit: www.aus.com/offices.

jobs.description:
Job Summary
The Campus Security Officer provides security and safety support for the Dallas campus.
Compensation
  • Regular shift: $16.80 per hour
  • Midnight shift: $18.30 per hour (includes shift differential)
Duties/Responsibilities
  • Patrol campus, check buildings, residential facilities, and parking lots; identify and address unauthorized individuals.
  • Interact with people.
  • Provide an armed, visible security presence on Campus.
  • Issue parking decals, perform computer work, and complete administrative tasks.
  • Investigate incidents, write reports, and respond to calls for service.
  • Respond to calls for service
  • Observe and report safety issues.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong interpersonal and customer service skills.
  • Ability to analyze situations quickly, make sound decisions, and function effectively in stressful environments.
  • High attention to detail and strong problem-solving skills.
  • Flexible schedule with willingness to work alone and serve as a self-starter.
  • Ability to follow directions while exercising good judgment.
  • Valid driver’s license with a good driving record.
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite or related software.
  • Must have or be able to obtain and maintain a valid Texas Level 3 (Commissioned) Armed Security Officer license (requires successful completion of required Level 2 and Level 3 training through a Texas DPS-approved provider)
Education and Experience:
  • A college degree preferred.
Physical Requirements:
  • Ability to climb, walk, balance, kneel, reach, lift up to 50 pounds, talk, and hear.
  • Comfort working in varying outside weather conditions, including during inclement weather when other officers may be unable to reach campus.

USA Patrol Division specializes in providing armed security services across various regions, including and. We are dedicated to serving government contracts and collaborating with local agencies to ensure safety and security for our communities.

In this role, you will be responsible for maintaining a safe environment by monitoring premises, managing access points, and responding swiftly to incidents. Your expertise in surveillance, conflict management, and emergency response will be vital in protecting property, assets, and personnel.

We value proactive individuals who bring energy, focus, and integrity to every shift — ensuring safety is always our top priority.

jobs.description: General Statement of Duties Please be sure to read the "Minimum Qualifications" section carefully to ensure you complete all requirements for a complete application. Candidates who do not comply with these requirements will not be considered for a position. This is a continuous recruitment and will remain open until the position is filled. For best consideration, apply by May 25, 2026; applications received after this date are not guaranteed a review. Performs police patrol and community peace keeping services related to civil matters; warrant service; investigations; traffic enforcement; ordinance enforcement and related law enforcement activities. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES - Works varying, rotating shifts performing service oriented police work, responding promptly to all types of service calls. - Conducts preventive patrols for crime prevention and detection. - Conducts traffic patrol and enforcement. - Responds to traffic crashes and other accidents, rendering aid and completing investigations of incidents. - Investigates criminal activity, including basic crime scene investigation, searching for and locating physical evidence. - Responds to animal control calls for service and occasionally may impound stray dogs when an assigned Animal Control Officer is unavailable or needs assistance. - Responds to other emergency service incidents as needed and provides first aid to injured persons as required. - Required to use proper judgment and available resources to complete tasks under high stress and in potential danger of physical injury. May include but is not limited to incidents involving arresting person(s) for felony or misdemeanor crimes and proper use of varying levels of force, ranging from presence to lethal. May include being verbally abused or physically assaulted and dealing with emotionally traumatic events. - Required to detail, in report form, actions and observations related to investigations and other tasks performed at work. Must be able to recall the details of work related actions and testify to same. - Required to issue citations as needed, accurately complete documents required by the Oregon Department of Motor Vehicles, Oregon Liquor Control Commission and other regulatory authorities as appropriate. May be required to testify to the content and details related to those documents, sometimes years later. - Must be able to identify evidence and process it in accordance with instruction. When no instruction has been provided, must be able to apply standards and training to improvise an appropriate way to collect and process evidence. - Must be able to coordinate activities with supervisors, other officers, other agencies, other City departments and citizens as needed. - Must be able to effectively communicate with prosecutors to seek advice on matters of law and procedure. - Must be able to act as an effective liaison between the Dallas Police Department, other agencies, local businesses and the community. - Interviews witnesses, suspects, and drivers. - Must be able to learn how to properly operate a mobile data computer system, mobile video recording system and other basic, law enforcement related technology. - Required to maintain the reasonable cleanliness of department vehicles being operated, including the interior and exterior. - Performs duties in conformance with applicable federal, state, county and city laws and ordinances and adheres to department policies and procedures and the law enforcement code of ethics. Ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with peers, subordinates, supervisors, and the general public. - Ability to follow written and verbal instruction. - Ability to exercise sound judgment. (NTN). To schedule a test, go to www.nationaltestingnetwork.com, select Law Enforcement, and sign up for the Dallas, Oregon Police Department. Upon completion of the entry level exam and ORPAT testing, all candidate scores are automatically forwarded to the Dallas Police Department. Candidates who attain a passing score on both the entry level exam and ORPAT will be placed on the department's eligibility list. The Dallas Police Department will contact candidates on this list to invite them to continue the selection process. If you have already completed the ORPAT and/or the Police Officer Selection Test with another agency within the last year, you may submit those results on agency letterhead in lieu of testing with NTN. If an applicant is 1) currently an Oregon law enforcement officer; OR 2) is currently a certified law enforcement officer in a U.S. state other than Oregon and meets the definition below for a lateral entry candidate, the candidate is not required to submit a POST or NTN Frontline test result if they can demonstrate they already completed such a test for their current employment as a police officer. A "lateral entry candidate" is defined as a person who can become an Oregon certified police officer without attending the DPSST Basic Police Course. jobs.title: Event Security Officers – Level II & Level III
jobs.description:
We are seeking professional, dependable, and experienced security officers to support event operations alongside event staff, venue security, local law enforcement.

Positions Available

  • Level II Non-Commissioned Security Officers
  • Level III Commissioned Security Officers

Level II Non-Commissioned Security OfficerPosition Summary

Level II Officers will provide professional, uniformed security support throughout the event. Officers will primarily be assigned to access-control, observation, guest-flow, and security-presence posts.

Responsibilities

  • Staff assigned security posts, including entrances, interior doorways, stairwells, corridors, registration areas, and other designated locations.
  • Maintain a professional and visible security presence.
  • Monitor assigned areas for unauthorized access, disturbances, suspicious activity, safety concerns, or violations of event policies.
  • Assist with orderly guest movement and crowd flow.
  • Provide basic directions and assistance to guests when appropriate.
  • Report security incidents or concerns through the established chain of command.
  • Assist event leadership, venue security, and law enforcement personnel as directed.
  • Respond appropriately to disturbances, safety concerns, or medical incidents until relieved by emergency personnel.
  • Remain at your assigned post unless properly relieved or directed otherwise.
  • Complete required incident documentation.

Important: Event personnel, not Level II officers, will have primary responsibility for validating invitations and checking guest identification.

Level II Requirements

  • Current Texas DPS Non-Commissioned Security Officer (Level II) license, or higher applicable Texas security license.
  • Must be eligible for affiliation with RKSMS through the Texas Online Private Security system prior to the event.
  • Must have completed all required Texas training and licensing requirements.
  • Level II officers will not carry firearms while performing security duties.
  • Professional appearance and conduct.
  • Strong communication and situational-awareness skills.
  • Ability to remain standing and attentive for extended periods.

Level III Commissioned Security OfficerPosition Summary

Level III Officers will provide armed security coverage at strategically designated locations throughout the event. Officers will supplement Level II personnel and support areas requiring an elevated security presence and rapid-response capability.

Responsibilities

  • Staff designated armed-security posts at higher-risk or strategically important locations.
  • Maintain a professional and highly visible armed-security presence.
  • Monitor assigned areas for threats, disturbances, unauthorized access, suspicious activity, and safety concerns.
  • Provide immediate security response when directed by event leadership.
  • Assist with de-escalation and management of security incidents within the officer's authority and training.
